observation.visible_scene: A transparent teardrop/egg-shaped glass object stands centered on a small metallic base (with three visible bolt heads) atop a white circular platform, against a uniform gray backdrop. Suspended inside the glass is a flat, rectangular wafer-like element covered in fine parallel diagonal ridges; these ridges diffract light into bright iridescent rainbow bands. The outer glass outline, the white platform edge, the bolted base, and the gray background remain fixed in frame throughout.
visible_changes: The internal ridged wafer rotates steadily about a vertical axis: its broad striped face seen in frame 1 (diagonal ridges tilted one way, rainbow band hugging the right edge) turns progressively toward edge-on by the final frames, where the wafer appears as a much narrower vertical strip with the rainbow concentrated near the center.

As the wafer rotates, the apparent tilt direction of its diagonal ridges reverses partway through the segment (ridges slanting lower-left to upper-right early, then upper-left to lower-right in the middle frames, then back again), consistent with continuous rotation rather than a single swing.

The distribution and hue of the diffracted rainbow shift frame to frame—magenta/cyan on the right early on, spreading across the whole wafer mid-segment, then narrowing to a bright central column late—tracking the changing viewing angle of the ridged surface.
A set of thin horizontal lines near the top of the internal element moves vertically and changes visibility as the element rotates.

The bright white specular patches on the left and right of the glass shell stay in roughly the same screen positions across all frames, indicating fixed lighting reflections rather than surface features of a rotating shell.
outside_clip_unknowns: The mechanism driving the rotation (e.g., a motorized turntable) is not shown.
Whether the excerpt captures a full rotation period or only part of one is unknown; the first and last wafer orientations do not match.
What lies beyond the cropped frame edges and the source of the studio lighting are unseen.
uncertain_details: It cannot be determined from the outline (the teardrop is near-rotationally symmetric and the white patches are fixed reflections) whether the outer glass shell itself rotates or only the internal wafer rotates within a stationary shell.
Camera motion is not evident—the background and platform are static—so the observed change is treated as object rotation, but slight camera drift cannot be fully excluded.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
